text.p: Shares of Employee Solutions Inc fell Friday after the provider of temporary workers confirmed market fears that its fiscal fourth quarter earnings would not live up to expectations.

Traders dumped the stock, sending it 9-1/2 lower to 5-7/8, its lowest level in 15 months. The stock was the most heavily traded on Nasdaq with over 27 million shares changing hands. The Phoenix, Ariz.-based company had about 33 million shares outstanding at the end of its fiscal third quarter.
The fall came hard on the heels of a drop of 5-/38 to $15-3/8 on Thursday. Just two weeks ago the company's stock reached its all-time high of 28-3/8.
"The comment that I keep hearing is that Employee Solutions was bleeding on Thursday and on Friday it has already bled to death," said Stacy Kleven, an analyst at TIS Group that follows the company.
Employee Solutions said Friday before the stock market opened that while it would still turn a profit for its fourth quarter and year-end, it would fall short of analysts expectations.
The company did not specify how low the profit would be.
Analysts had expected the company would earn $0.14 a share for the quarter and $0.44 for the year, according to First Call.
"The rumor is that the numbers are going to be quite bad," Kleven said, although she declined to estimate now bad the profits might be. "It's got to be pretty bad."

"This company has such a high short interest out there, and they're probably laughing all the way to the bank, and this is a heavy rumor stock and a lot of the traders are just self-perpetuating the rumors to drive the stock down," she said.

On Thursday, after the company said it would delay its earnings release, a source close to the company said the delay was caused by the problems associated with collating results given the company's heavy acquisition activity throughout the year.
